_note: Quenya interface, and **it is 30% of the catalogue rather than 100%, which is the finding rather than a shortfall**. The rest of the keys are absent, so they fall back to English: `data/i18n/` is a partial-overlay design by construction -- "a key it omits falls back to English rather than rendering a bare key, so a half-translated language degrades to a mixed interface instead of a broken one" -- and this is the first language that has needed that property for a reason other than being unfinished. SOURCE: every root is attested in Tolkien's Late Quenya, taken from Eldamo's `l="q"` set with no reliability mark or with `#` (derivable from an attested form by a grammatical rule). Inflected forms are regular compositions on those roots -- `lambi` the plural of `lambë`, `hentalyë` the 2nd-person polite of `henta-`, `tengwaron` the genitive plural of `tengwa` -- which Eldamo does not index because it indexes lemmas, and their absence from the index is therefore not evidence. What IS evidence is a *root* being absent, and that is what cut this catalogue in half: `hep-` (keep, for Save), `cil-` (choose, for the two Choose-a-face controls -- only the noun `cilmë` "choice" survives), `mauya-` (compel, for Essential and for "both fields are needed"), `valdë` (worth, for Priority and Importance), `munta` (nothing, for four separate empty-state strings), `nossë` (family), `nótë` (number), `palúrë` (surface, for Card width), `cirissë` (slash, for Divider), `erya` (sole), `vére` (own, for Custom), and `tengwal` -- twelve roots that a Neo-Quenya writer would supply from the reconstructed lexicon and that Tolkien did not. `holya-` "to shut" exists and is excluded too: Eldamo marks it `?`, meaning speculative, so the Close button has no verb. There is also **no attested Quenya word for column, for row, for size, for colour as an abstraction, for print, for page, or for translate**, which is most of a format panel. REGISTER: the imperative particle `á` before the verb stem, which is Tolkien's own construction (`á vala Manwë`, `á tule`, `á hyamë`) and the only imperative Quenya has. So buttons read `á napanë` "add", `á lelta` "send", `á cenë` "look at". `áva` for a negative imperative, likewise attested. TERMS: `parma` is a book or written document and stands in for the sheet; `cendelë` is a face, and using it for a printed side is the same metaphor English makes, flagged here as the one extension of sense in the catalogue. Also: `tengwa` = letter, `tengwar` = the letters, `quetta` = word, `lambë` = language, `canta` = shape or framework, for the Format panel; `nat` = thing, `nati` = the items; `lantalca` = boundary mark, which is exactly a margin; `asta` = a division or part, for a section; `raxë` = danger, for the emergency colour; `lúmë` = time; `men` = way. INTERPOLATION -- and Quenya is the sharpest case in the whole project. A placeholder is a plain string substitution, and **Quenya's ten cases are all suffixal and all have allomorphs chosen by the stem's final sound**: the instrumental is `-nen` after a vowel and `-inen` after a consonant, the allative `-nna` assimilates to `-nda` after `-n`, the plural is `-r` after a vowel and `-i` otherwise. So a template may never put a case suffix after a placeholder, and the first draft of this file did it five times: `{language}nen`, `{regions}ssë`, `{faces}llo`, `{total}llo`. Every one is now a bare noun beside a dash or an adjacent head word -- `i nassë — {language}`, `{language} parma` -- so the grammar hangs off Quenya's own word and the insert stays inert. That is the same repair the Hungarian and Indonesian catalogues record, and Quenya needs it more than either, because Hungarian's `-ban/-ben` at least fails audibly where Quenya's would produce a form that looks like a different case. The article is the second trap and it is avoided the same way: `i` is invariable, so it is safe before a placeholder, but the adjective agreement is not -- a plural adjective takes `-ë` or `-i` depending on its own shape, so no template here puts an adjective in agreement with an inserted noun. Serif and Sans and the romanisation-system names stay Latin, as in the Greek and Indonesian catalogues. INTERFACE-STRINGS PASS -- the forty-seven editor./speaker./speech./personal./settings. keys, of which **twenty-six are here and twenty-one are not**, which is the widest gap in the catalogue and is the finding. NEW ROOTS, every one Eldamo l="q" with no reliability mark unless stated: `eques` "saying, dictum, a quotation from someone's uttered words" (WJ/392.3511, stem equess-, plural `equessi` attested at WJ/392.3603) -- **this is the word the whole editor family turns on**, because Quenya has no word for a button and none for a sentence, and an eques is exactly what one of these buttons holds; `véra` "personal, private, own" (PM/340.2707), which the note above wrongly listed as missing under the headword `vére` -- the adjective is attested and the noun is not; `óma` "voice" (LotR/0377.3401, Namárië, plural `ómar` on the attested `ómainen` WJ/391.3200); `senya` "usual" (VT49/22.0602, and `ve senya` "as usual" at VT49/06.0900); `tanna` "sign, token" (MR/385.2903); `pá` "touching, against, on; as regards, concerning" (VT44/26.3504); `orta-` "to raise, lift up" (Let/426.3415) and `núta-` "to lower" (PE22/156.0905); `telya-` "to finish, wind up, conclude" (WJ/411.2709); `ambë` "more" (PE17/091.0214); `ahya-` "to change" (PM/395.1303, mark #, attested in *manen lambë Quendion ahyanë*); `elyë` (LotR/0378.0202); `-ltë` "they" (PE17/075.4403), used in `cenuvaltë` on the model of attested *hiruvalyë*. WHAT IS NOT HERE, and it is twenty-one keys. **There is no Quenya verb for `write`**: `tek-` is ᴹQ only (Ety/TEK.012) and Late Quenya keeps only the noun `tecil` "pen" (PM/318.4207) and `sarmë` "writing" (VT39/08.3411). **There is no verb for `translate`**: `lambelanga-` and `pahtalanga-` are ᴺQ, marked ! -- pure fan inventions. **There is no verb for `save`**: `hep-` is ᴺQ ! (PE14/056.1502); `öa-`/`auta-²` "to possess, own, keep" (PE22/151.2904) is stative possession, so `á öa` would read *possess it!*; `rehta-` (PE17/038.2405) is *rescue*, not *store*. **There is no noun for `nothing`**: `munta` is ᴺQ from PE14 -- the corpus row numbers-money.l-ng carries it under `qya-earlier-v1` at confidence 1, which is that file's licence and not this one's. **There is no word for a screen, a page or a panel**: the only attested `fanwa` is a veil (PE17/176.1003). **There is no word for a device, a computer, a machine or a browser**: `carma` and `tamma` are a tool or implement (PE17/114.3105, PE17/108.0404) and a phone is not one. And there is no `some` as a quantifier of a plural, no `neither`, no `until`, no `set`/`configure`, no `copy`, no `connection`, no `aloud`, no `guess` fit for the sentence, and no `forget`. So: editor.noTranslation, editor.noListenerText, editor.save, editor.removeHere, editor.confirmDeleteMany, editor.none, speaker.lede, speaker.nothingToAsk, speaker.unset, speech.remote-only, speech.unsupported, personal.lede, personal.export, personal.import, personal.confirm, personal.nothing, personal.loaded, personal.refused all fall back to English. THREE OF THE TWENTY-ONE ARE REFUSED FOR A DIFFERENT REASON, and it is the more interesting one. editor.removeHere ("Remove from this screen") is left out not only because there is no word for a screen but because without one it is indistinguishable from editor.delete, and two buttons with one label is worse than one of them in English. personal.forget ("Delete everything") would be `á aucirë ilya` -- **which is already studio.allOff word for word**, and studio.allOff only turns print sections off while personal.forget destroys the reader's data; the same string on both is a hazard, so the destructive one stays English. settings.open and settings.title are out because Quenya has exactly one word here, `cilmë` "choice" (MR/470.2101), and it is already spent twice, on quick.optionsLabel and board.menu -- a third control with the same label is worse than an English one. personal.heading still says `cilmi` because it is inside a longer phrase there and cannot be mistaken for either control. SEVEN STRINGS ARE REWORDED rather than translated. editor.title is `vérë equessi` "personal sayings" and editor.open `á vista i equessi` "change the sayings": there is no word for *button*, and the editor family is therefore written about the saying rather than the control that shows it -- which is the same repair the Klingon catalogue makes with mu'tlhegh, and for the same reason. editor.label is `senta tanna`, "short sign": there is no word for *label*, and `tanna` (MR/385.2903) is the nearest attested one -- `tengwa` is glossed "sign, token, indicator" too but this catalogue has already spent it on *letter*. `senta` "short" is PE17/141.3404 and is Eldamo's preferred Late Quenya form of the three (ᴹQ `sinta`, Ety/STINTĀ; `senna`, PE17/185). editor.owner and editor.listener are the bare `lambelya` and `hyana lambë`, "your language" and "the other language", because there is no verb *to mean*; `lambelya` is the exact counterpart of field.gloss's `lambenya`. editor.damaged keeps all three of the English's moves and loses none -- `Lá polin henta i equessi` is communication.i-cannot-read-it's own words, `Sinomë ëar` "here they are" carries *nothing has been overwritten* with `ëar`, the plural this file already writes at ornament.hint, and `Ála napanë ambë` is the instruction. speech.loading is `I ómar tulir…`, "the voices are coming", which is gallery.loading's `i lambi tulir…` unchanged, and it drops *try again in a moment*. speech.synthesis-failed drops *try again* and keeps the other two clauses, in room-problems' subject-`ná`-adjective shape. THE PAIR THE LANGUAGE NEARLY COLLAPSES. speech.no-voice and speech.unmapped are the same sentence apart from one word, because there is no noun for a device: `Sinomë lá ëa tana lambëo óma` "here there is no voice of that language" against `Lá ëa tana lambëo óma` "there is no voice of that language". `sinomë` is the corpus's own word for *in this place* and is doing the work *on this device* does in English; the two stay distinguishable, which is the whole point of having both, and the distinction is weaker than the Klingon one. ONE COLLAPSE THE LANGUAGE FORCES: speaker.speaker_gender.why says `Sinë lambissen ahyar i quettar pá elyë`, "in these languages the words about you change", where the English says "a verb or an adjective". Quenya has no noun for either -- Eldamo's l="q" set holds the suffixes (-ya, -ina, -ië, -lë) and no word for the classes themselves -- and coining two to translate a sentence about other languages would be the invention this file does not make. The English's two examples go with them. GRAMMAR, checked rather than assumed: no placeholder in any of these twenty-six carries a suffix, which is the rule at the head of this note; the only string with a placeholder is speaker.unspecified's neighbour speaker.unset, and that one is absent. SECTION TITLES, in data/registry/section-titles/qya.csv: nine of the fifty-two that were missing are now there, and forty-three are not. `omentië` (introductions) is boards.intro.title unchanged; `auri` (days-of-week) is board.days unchanged; `astar` (months) is the plural of Tolkien's own calendar word `asta` "month" (LotR/1108.2109), which is the same word this catalogue spends on *section* at addTerm.section, because LotR/1108 glosses it "month; division, part" and both senses are his -- and `astar` is also a separate noun "faith, loyalty" (PE17/183.2602), a homograph that is left standing because the card prints it over Narvinyë to Ringarë, where nothing else it could mean survives contact with the list; `equessi` (utility-templates) is "sayings", the plural attested at WJ/392.3603; `híni` (children) is the plural of `hína` (PE17/157.1405); `nómi` (place-words) is the plural of `nómë` "place" (VT42/17, mark #, the element inside sinomë and tanomë); `notië` (numbers-money) is "counting" (VT48/11.2907, mark #, implied by *maquanotië*), and it heads that section because every one of its fourteen Quenya rows is a numeral -- there is no attested noun for *number* (`nótë` is absent) and none for *money*; `raxë` (trail-warnings) is colour.alert unchanged, and it is free for the trail because emergency-medical has no Quenya rows at all; `hanquentar` (board-answers) is the plural of board.reply's `hanquenta`. NINETEEN OF THE FORTY-THREE ARE EMPTY SECTIONS -- phone-translation, phone-text-power, sim-data, profanity, payment-receipt, dietary-needs, tax-refund, attractions-tickets, taxi, transit-rides, hotel-words, hotel-requests, laundry, pickup-meeting, emergency-medical, medical-conditions, pharmacy-symptoms, lost-rescue and massage-spa have no Quenya rows, and a heading over nothing is worse than no heading. The rest are lexical. There is no attested word for *weather* (fifteen rows, the largest headless section: `vilya` is air and `menel` the firmament, and neither names heat, cold or flood); none for *greeting* (`suila-` is ᴺQ), which leaves social-basics; none for *slang*, *etiquette* or *tipping*; none for a *toilet*; none for *train*, *rail* or *station*; and `sambë` "room" is ᴹQ (Ety/STAB.005), which is why hotel-basics and room-problems have none. Four more are collisions rather than gaps: quick-responses would be `hanquentar` too, time-scheduling would be `lúmë`, which is already time-words, quick-directions would be `men`, which is already directions, and trail-landmarks would be `tengwar`, which is already common-signs -- in each pair English has two names and Quenya one, and the second card would repeat the first. question-words is left out although `maquetië` could be built on `maquet-` (PM/403.0811, mark #): the section is half question words and half particles -- *a little*, *very*, *also*, *all* -- and a heading reading "questioning" would misname half of what is printed under it. TWO INFLECTIONS WORTH NAMING, both regular and neither indexed. `lambissen` is the plural locative of `lambë` on the attested `lassissen` pattern. `sinë` is the plural of the adjective `sina`, -a to -ë as `ilya`/`ilyë`; PE23/102-107 happens to spell a *singular* variant demonstrative `sine`, which is a different word from a different note and not evidence against the plural. STUDIO, EXPORT AND PREVIEW PASS -- the sixty format.head*/export./picker./popup./quick./preview.lock/studio.moreActions keys, of which **two are here and fifty-eight are not**, which is the widest gap yet and is again the finding rather than a shortfall. WHAT IS HERE. picker.sections is astar i parmassë "sections on the card": asta is what addTerm.section already calls a section and parma is what format.card and preview.cardLabel already call the card, and -ssë after a vowel is the regular locative. The astar/"faith, loyalty" homograph (PE17/183.2602) is the one this note already accepted for the months title, and the argument is the same: it sits over a grid of section chips, where nothing else it could mean survives contact with the label. preview.lockDate is Isilya 15 Yavannië -- **the one string in this pass Quenya is better placed to write than any natural language**, because Tolkien published both a weekday list and a month list and data/lang/qya/time.csv already carries them at confidence 3: Isilya is Monday at LotR/1110.2813 and Yavannië is September at LotR/1110.0309. The day number stays a digit, as it does on a lock screen, and the order mirrors the English because Quenya date order is not attested. preview.lockTime is left out although Intl refuses this tag: 9:41 is digits and a colon, the English floor is therefore already the right rendering, and repeating it would only hide the fact that nothing was decided. WHAT IS NOT HERE, fifty-eight keys, and the reasons are the ones the head of this note already lists. No verb for **save** (hep- is ᴺQ !, öa-/auta-² is stative possession, rehta- is rescue), so export.savePage, export.saveAll and the whole export box go; no word for **print**, **page** or a **screen**, which takes export.pages, export.asZip, quick.imageOf, quick.docTitle, quick.status, quick.statusScreen, quick.subtitle, quick.typesetting and format.reserveHint; no word for **row**, which takes picker.budget, picker.budgetTitle, popup.showRow and popup.editing; no **munta** "nothing", which takes quick.nothing and quick.nothingToExport; no word for **colour as an abstraction**, which takes format.headColour and format.headFillOne; and no word for **text**, which takes format.headSlot.custom, format.headTextPlaceholder and popup.editText. THREE NEW REFUSALS THAT ARE NOT SIMPLY A MISSING NOUN. (1) **There is no Quenya word for a tab**, none for a corner and none for a strip, so the eighteen format.headFill / format.headReach / format.headSpan keys and their titles all go together, on the same reasoning the Klingon note gives for the same eighteen. (2) **There is no attested verb "to show"**: Eldamo's Late Quenya index offers only leptenta- "to point to, indicate with finger", and the one verb for opening is latya- "to open anything (so as to allow entry)", which is about admitting entry and not about displaying a saved file -- so popup.showRow, popup.showSection, popup.showInList and export.openPage are out, and so is studio.moreActions, there being no noun for an action either. (3) **gallery.converse cannot be written, and the reason is a deprecation rather than a gap.** carpa- "to talk, speak, use tongue" is on Eldamo's Neo-Quenya deprecated list -- √KARAP was probably replaced by √PAKAT (PE17/126) -- and this file does not use deprecated forms, which is already why board.reply is the noun hanquenta rather than one of aquet-/tóquet-/endaquet-. The only sound speech verb left is quet-, and it is already spent on board.speak as á quetë; putting it on the gallery card as well would give two different controls one label, which is the hazard settings.open and personal.forget are already absent for. gallery.tagline goes with it: the sentence needs design, save and print in its first half alone. MESSAGE-SCREEN PASS -- the twelve board.slow / board.switch* / display.* keys, of which **eleven are here and one is not**, and four of the eleven are rewordings. NEW ROOTS, every one Eldamo l="q" with no reliability mark unless stated: `enquet-` "to repeat, say again" (PE17/167.0712), which is board.slow's verb and exactly its sense; `lintië` "swiftness, speed" (PE17/058.3310), whose instrumental Tolkien himself wrote in *nornë lintieryanen* "he ran with his speed" (PE17/058.3811), so `lintienen` is his case on his noun; `per-` "half-" (Let/386.0906, mark #, from *Pereldar*), a prefix and used here only as one -- `perlintienen` "at half speed" is the single new compound in this catalogue and is flagged as such. board.slow is therefore `á enquetë perlintienen`. board.switchLanguage is `á vista i lambë`. board.switchTopic is `á vista i asta`: there is no word for a topic, and `asta` "division, part" (LotR/1108.2109) is what addTerm.section and picker.sections already call one; the three sit on three different surfaces, so the reuse never puts one label on two neighbouring controls. display.voice is `óma`; display.voiceAuto "chosen automatically" is reworded to `i senya óma` "the usual voice", because there is no verb *choose* (`cil-` is absent, as the head of this note records) and no *automatic*, and `senya` is what speaker.unspecified already uses for the standard wording. THE FIVE CHECKBOXES name things the screen can show, and Quenya has no noun for a button, a control, a romanisation or a screen, so each names the thing itself: display.owner `lambelya nu i eques` "your language, under the saying" (editor.owner's `lambelya`, `nu` as in the margin handles, `eques` as throughout the editor); display.roman `quetië — Latin tengwar` and display.ipa `quetië — IPA`, where `quetië` is field.respell's own word and *Latin* stays Latin as the romanisation-system names do -- "in your own letters" is deliberately not translated, because a Quenya reader's own letters are tengwar and that line shows Latin ones; display.speak `á quetë ar 0.5×`, the two controls' own faces joined by `ar`, because "the half-speed button beside it" has no noun to hang on and that button's face is a numeral in every language; display.turn `á querë i tengwar`, board.turn word for word, for the same reason. display.heading is reworded to `i nati as i eques`, "the things with the saying" (`nati` from studio.contentPanel; `as` "with", VT43/29.1101, mark #, as in *i Héru as elyë*), because "what the message screen shows" has neither *screen* nor the *show* it needs. WHAT IS NOT HERE: display.lede, the one paragraph. It needs *screen*, *hold out*, *turn off*, *turn on* and *pronunciation*, none of which exists, and a two-word stub over five checkboxes would say less than the English does. ONE CORRECTION to the studio pass above: it says "there is no attested verb to show", but Eldamo's l="q" set does carry `tana-` "to show, indicate" (MR/471.3501, unmarked), the verb under `tanna` "sign". It is not spent in this pass -- the popup./export. keys it would unlock are outside it, and *show* in display.heading means *display on a surface*, which is a different sense -- but the next agent to touch those keys should start from `tana-` and not from that sentence.
quick.heading: {language} parma
ornament.hint: Vanyë lantalcar. I tengwar ar i canta lá ahyar. Cantar mi i cendeli, yassë lá ëar tengwar.
ornament.frameHint: Canta Eldaron. Lantalcar ar cendeli polir ahya.
ornament.lowInk: Morna pitya: i yára. I canta entulë as morna ar fanya, hya as luinë, carnë ar laica.
_ornament_note: Style strings are editorial compositions, not quotations from Tolkien. They paraphrase technical terms using the Late Quenya vocabulary indexed at https://eldamo.org/content/word-indexes/words-q.html: canta (shape), rembina (woven), falma (wave), ondo (stone), lasse (leaf), ahya- (change), entul- (return). Woven ribbon is rendered as woven shapes; laurel manuscript as document and leaves; Starforge as stars and iron. The hint says beautiful boundary marks, unchanged letters and framework, and shapes on faces where there are no letters. Low ink is little black; colour is paraphrased with blue, red and green, alongside black and white for monochrome. These metaphors avoid inventing words for modern print terminology.
_board_note: Conversation-board and beacon strings: six of the ten, for the reason the rest of this file is partial -- the root is not there. SOURCES, as elsewhere here, are Eldamo's Late Quenya set: asya- "to ease, assist, comfort" (PE17/148), nin "for me" (LotR/0377), appa- "to touch" (VT44/26), tel- "to end, finish" (WJ/411; teluva is its regular future), ar "and" (LotR/0377), hanquenta "answer" (PE17/166), tancata- "to make firm, fix, confirm" (PE17/076), hyana "other" (VT49/14), lume "time, period of time, hour" (LotR/0081, PE17/013), and the imperative particle a (Let/448). beacon.help is á asya nin "help me", the phrase data/lang/qya/building.csv already carries at accessibility.help-me-carry; this pack has no emergency-medical.help row to align with. board.reply is the noun hanquenta and not an imperative, because all three attested verbs for "to answer" -- aquet-, tóquet-, endaquet- -- are forms Eldamo marks deprecated. beacon.dismiss is reworded to á appa ar teluva, "touch and it will end", there being no word for "anywhere". board.amount is malca lúmë "how much time", which the corpus already composes at time-scheduling.how-long-does-it-take: malca is Middle Quenya (PE22/124) rather than Late, the one form in this file outside the l="q" set, and it is flagged here rather than left to be found. WHAT IS NOT HERE, and falls back to English by design: board.close, for the reason the main note gives -- holya- "to shut" is marked ? and this file does not use it; board.unit and board.notAnAmount, because Quenya has no attested word for a minute and none for a number, nótë being one of the twelve roots listed above that Tolkien never supplied; and beacon.sos, because SOS is a Morse sequence and not an abbreviation of words, so the Latin letters stand. SECOND PASS -- six keys for a clock and a bare number, of which two are reachable and four are not. board.atTime is lúmessë, the locative of lúmë, attested at VT43/34 in Tolkien's Quenya Ave Maria -- sí ar lúmessë ya firuvammë "now and at the hour of our death" -- and it says what the English "At a time" says, preposition and all. board.time is mana i lúmë "what is the hour", the form data/lang/qya/time.csv already carries at time-scheduling.what-time-is-it, taken the same way board.amount was taken from how-long-does-it-take. WHAT IS NOT HERE, on top of the three above: board.number, board.otherNumber and board.notANumber, for the reason board.notAnAmount is already absent -- nótë is one of the twelve roots listed above that Tolkien never supplied; and board.notATime, because cil- "to choose" is another of them, and only the noun cilmë survives. Worth recording, because it is not obvious: the clock is reachable even though board.unit is not, since the minute/hour/day buttons are drawn for a duration only and a time of day therefore never needs a Quenya word for a minute. THIRD PASS -- the fifty-four conversation-board and page-chrome strings, of which twenty-two are reachable and thirty-two are not, a shade better than the rest of this file. SOURCES, Eldamo's Late Quenya l="q" index as before: quet- "to say, speak, tell" (PE17/126; SA/quen) for board.speak á quetë; quer- "to turn" (VT49/20) for board.turn á querë i tengwar, the verb gallery.previewSwap already spends; entul- "to come again, return" (CPT/1296 entule, S/195 entuluva) for board.up; cilmë "choice, choosing" (MR/470; PE22/149) for board.menu i cilmi -- the phrase quick.optionsLabel already carries, and what a menu is; ilya "all" (LotR/0377) with lambë (PM/395) for board.toGallery ilyë lambi, the phrase already under nav.back; ëa- "to be, exist" (PE17/074) with hanquenta "answer" (PE17/166) for board.canAnswer ëa hanquenta "there is an answer", a noun clause for the same reason board.reply is a noun -- all three attested verbs for "to answer" are deprecated; lúmë (LotR/0081) pluralised lúmi for board.hours, and aurë "day" (WJ/166; SA/ur) pluralised auri for board.days, aurë rather than ré because ré's plural is not securely derivable. THE EIGHT TITLES, six of which are reachable: raxë for boards.emergency.title, the word colour.alert already gives for the same English; men "way" (SA/men) for boards.directions.title, which is what data/registry/section-titles/qya.csv gives the directions section; lúmë for boards.time.title, likewise that file's title for time-words; matië "eating" for boards.food.title, the gerund quiz.interest.food already carries; omentië "meeting" (LotR/0081; Let/265) for boards.intro.title; and lenda "journey" (PE17/060) for boards.transport.title. **lenda is a deliberate disagreement with colour.move, which renders the same English "Getting around" as men.** Both cannot be men: boards.directions.title and boards.transport.title are two tiles on one eight-tile grid, and two identical tiles is a worse fault than one title differing from a colour-role label on another screen. boards.shopping.title and boards.spa.title have no word at all -- the index has nothing for buying, trade or a market, and nothing for massage. ALSO COMPOSED from attested pieces: vanwa "gone, lost" (LotR/0377) for boards.emergency.lost, which drops "or stolen" because no Late Quenya verb for stealing survives; á nyarë "tell" (nyar-, PE18/094) for boards.emergency.conditionsTitle; lá "no, not" (PE22/160; VT49/13) with polin, the attested aorist 1sg of pol- "can" (PE17/155), and matë, the aorist infinitive of mat- "to eat" (PE22/131), for boards.food.avoid lá polin matë… -- the same frame ornament.hint already uses at lá ahyar; ma, the interrogative particle (PE17/068), with ëa for boards.food.contains ma ëa… "is there…", which is data/lang/qya/food.csv's own composition at food-ordering.does-it-contain minus the slot; and ma polin matë sina "can I eat this" for boards.food.containsTitle, there being no attested word for safe. boards.emergency.sos is á tinta SOS, tinta- "to kindle, cause to spark" (PE17/069), with SOS left Latin for the reason the first pass gives. **That is the second extension of sense in this file after cendelë**, and it is flagged the same way: Tolkien's word is for kindling a spark, not for a screen that blinks. WHAT IS NOT HERE, thirty-two keys, all falling back to English by design. There is no attested word for: a topic or a context (board.allTopics, board.pickTopic); to translate, as the main note records (board.someMissing, board.unavailable, board.wrongPair); a conversation or a board (board.docTitle, board.noBoards); a minute, as the first pass records (board.minutes); to shut, holya- being marked ? (board.dismiss); attention (boards.emergency.attention); to be ill or an illness -- the index offers only saura and úmara, adjectives glossed "bad, unhealthy" (boards.emergency.medical, boards.emergency.conditions); wrong (boards.emergency.medicalTitle); to focus (boards.spa.focus, boards.spa.focusOn); comfort (boards.spa.comfort); a ticket, a platform, a taxi, a bus or a train (all six boards.transport.* under the title); munta "nothing", already on the twelve-root list (boards.food.avoidTitle); and hep- "to keep", likewise, whose absence takes boards.spa.justRight, since "keep it there" is the whole point of that button. board.pair is left out because the English is an arrow and any translation would be the same string. THE SPLIT, and here it is broken rather than reordered: boards.spa.focusOn "Please focus on…" cannot be written, so the heading stays English, and of the four body parts under it only two exist -- lango "neck" (PE17/065) and táli, the attested plural of tál "foot" (PE16/096; PE19/103). Eldamo's Quenya index has no shoulder and no back as a body part -- nan- is a directional prefix and nanda "rear" an adjective -- so boards.body.shoulders and boards.body.back are absent. The two that are here stand as bare nouns and not as possessives: -nya "my" is attested (PE17/057) and langonya would be regular, but with the governing sentence in English and half the group missing, the bare noun is the honest form and the possessive would be decoration on a sentence that is not there.

_signal_note: Signal-in-Morse pass (drill.reveal, format.headSlot.logo, gallery.signal, board.rate, signal.*): ten of thirteen keys are here, three are not. REUSE: tinta- "to kindle, set fire to" is boards.emergency.sos's own verb (á tinta SOS) and is spent again on gallery.signal and signal.start (á tinta), because Morse and the beacon are the same physical act on this phone -- a flashing light -- and Quenya's one word for it should not become two. telya- "to finish, wind up, conclude" (WJ/411.2709) is speaker.done's own verb (á telya) and is spent again on signal.stop, for the same reason. tanna "sign, token" (MR/385.2903) is editor.label's word and is spent twice more, on format.headSlot.logo (Phraselet tanna) and on signal.heading (Morse tanna), because a logo and a section heading are both signs and Quenya has the one word for it. hanquenta "answer" (board.reply) gives drill.reveal á cenë i hanquenta, cen- "to see" being the verb á cenë already uses at gallery.wantPick. lintië "speed" (PE17/058.3310) is board.slow's own noun, spent again bare at signal.speed and joined to quetië "speech, utterance" (already display.roman's word) with the same connector display.heading uses (as, "with") for board.rate: lintië as quetië, "speed with speech", avoiding any case ending on either noun. signal.message is vérë eques, on editor.title's own model (vérë equessi, "personal sayings") rather than a possessive suffix on eques, whose stem-final consonant (equess-) is not attested taking one. WHAT IS NOT HERE. signal.lede needs screen, phone, hold out, tap and lend, none of which is attested -- the same gap display.lede was left out for. signal.received and signal.unsayable both need code, which is not attested and cannot be built from anything already spent in this file (a code is not a sign, a mark or a saying); rather than force tanna or eques into a sense neither carries, both are absent. THE SECTION TITLE. There is no Quenya Wikipedia, so morse-code has no sourced term and no row was added to section-titles/qya.csv, on the same footing as the nineteen empty sections _note already lists -- a coined word here would be exactly the invention this file has avoided everywhere else. "Morse" itself is a modern Earth surname with no possible Quenya form; it is left in Latin throughout, the same treatment SOS, PNG and the roman.* system names already get.
